accounts.name: collection
docs: `permanent_freeze_delegate` sits on either an asset or a collection, and this pool's live
one sits on the collection, held by a third party. Without this
account the seizure this instruction exists for is undetectable: the card is present,
vault-owned and unfrozen in its own registry, so the read would answer `Settleable` and
refuse to close a position whose card MPL Core will not move.
**Pinned in the classification rather than here.** `Position` stores no collection, and
the asset's own `update_authority` is not readable at account-validation time, so
`read_collateral` requires this account to be exactly the asset's collection before
walking the registry; that stops a caller naming any frozen collection to seize a healthy
position. Never `mut`: read only, and no CPI.
The census walks this registry as well as the asset's, so it is also where a rejecting
`Royalties` rule set or an external adapter declaring a Transfer check can hide, which
makes the classification `Undecidable`. A `Royalties` record whose rule set is `None`
hides nothing and is `Clear`.

accounts.name: treasury_05
docs: The protocol-wide Treasury 05. It is the USDC associated token account of
`protocol_config.t05_authority`, so the address is *derived* here rather than read from a
stored field: owner and mint determine the one address, and there is no second config
value that could disagree with it.
**It must already exist.** Like `protocol_revenue`, this is a deployment-time account
rather than one that arrives with a caller, so it is pinned and not created here — the
idempotent creation this instruction does for a roller's $BYE account exists because a
roller shows up unpredictably, which is not true of either fee destination. A missing
Treasury 05 fails every settlement in every pool until someone creates the ATA; that is
a condition a retry clears, and anyone may create it permissionlessly.

Anchor resolves a seed expression against the declared field, and on an `Option` that
field is the `Option` itself, so `position.nft_mint` does not compile. The handler derives
every one of them from the stored bumps instead, which is both the binding and the only
place a reader has to look for it.
This instruction serves the Token Metadata family only, and the standard is asserted here
rather than in the handler so it runs **before any CPI** — a settlement moves USDC before
it touches the card, so a handler-side check would come after money had already left.

types.name: AcquiredActivated
docs: A treasury-acquired position entering the pool.
**Deliberately not a reuse of `DepositApproved`**: no attestation happens at activation. The
`value` and `observed_at` were attested when the card was bought and are only read back here,
so an approval event would record a value decision nobody made.
`observed_age_seconds` is `Clock.unix_timestamp − observed_at` in **seconds, not slots**, and
it is carried because the gap between attestation and activation is unbounded — this is the
field that makes that gap measurable rather than inferred.

types.name: AuthorityRole
docs: **`T05` occupies the wire byte (2) of Treasury 03's retired authority role**, which keeps
`T02` at 3: removing or reordering a variant re-decodes every `AuthorityRotated` in a
deployed cluster's logs as a different role. Logs predating the revival carry byte 2 under
the old role and read as `T05` now.

types.name: BatchClosed
docs: A settled or recovered batch's account closed and its rent returned. Nothing records the batch
after this, so the event is the only surviving statement that it existed and where its rent
went.

types.name: BatchCommitted
docs: A batch's commitment, carrying the priced terms it will settle on.
The five `s_*` fields are the snapshot the batch settles against no matter what a later
`update_config` does, and they are published here because a third party auditing a settlement
must read the terms that priced it rather than the pool's current ones. The set is the priced
terms **only** — the tier accrual denominator and Treasury 04's ceiling are read live at
settlement, so neither is snapshotted and neither belongs here.

types.name: BatchCompleted
docs: A batch reaching its last roll, releasing the actions gated on an open batch.
`open_batches_remaining` is the count **after** the decrement — carried so a watcher reads
the pool's freeze state off the event rather than reconstructing the count across events.
Commits queue, so a nonzero value means another batch is already committed and queued to
become the next head.

types.name: BatchRecovered
docs: A batch whose randomness never arrived, recovered after its timeout. `wallet` is what makes
per-wallet timeout rates computable, which is the anomaly signal that stands in for preventing
a withheld callback.
`open_batches_remaining` is the post-decrement count, carried for the same reason
[`BatchCompleted`] carries it — recovery is the other instruction that decrements it.

types.name: BatchResolved
docs: Randomness delivered for a batch. Carries no result of its own — it is the anchor an indexer
replays a batch's settlements forward from, which is why it names the batch even though the
callback writes only `randomness` and the state transition.

types.name: BatchState
docs: Where a batch sits in its lifecycle.
**Declaration order is the borsh wire byte**, not an implementation detail: a fieldless enum
serializes as its declaration index, so reordering these variants silently reinterprets every
already-written `RollBatch` and every client decode. Append only.

types.name: BuybackPayer
docs: Who paid for a sale. The declaration index is the wire byte.

types.name: CollectionAdmitted
docs: `old_standards` is `0` on a creation, so one event type covers both admitting a collection and
re-standarding an admitted one. `reason` is `Some` **exactly** when the update cleared a bit,
which is what puts the motive on chain rather than only at the instruction boundary.

types.name: CollectionWithdrawn
docs: Carries the withdrawn `standards` because nothing else survives the close: afterwards no
account records that this collection was ever admitted or what it permitted, so the admitted
set at any slot is reconstructible from events alone or not at all.

types.name: ConfigUpdate
docs: One configuration move. Independent parameters are scalar variants; the three coupled
surfaces are composites validated as a unit, since `fee == price - ticket_target`, the
10,000 allocation sum and the face array cannot be satisfied one parameter at a time.

types.name: ConfigValue
docs: A single scalar `Pool`/`ProtocolConfig` field value, old or new, as carried by `ConfigChanged`.

types.name: DepositPending
docs: `standard` is **appended last**, so no existing field's wire offset moves. This event and
`InstantSold` are the only two that carry the discriminant: they are the two intake points,
where the value is derived and where an indexer sources it from when it inserts the position
row.
It is also the only thing that separates this event's two emit sites. `deposit` and
`deposit_core` agree on every other field, so the discriminant is what says in the stream
which custody path an escrowed card took — and the Core custody monitor's sweep set is
exactly the positions it marks `STANDARD_CORE`.

types.name: Escrow
docs: A wallet's USDC escrow, one per owner and shared by every pool. Seeds: `[ESCROW_SEED, owner]`.
**It stores no balance.** The balance is the token amount of the vault at
`[ESCROW_VAULT_SEED, escrow]`, whose only authority is this PDA, so there is no second number
to drift from the first. USDC sent straight to the vault by a plain SPL transfer is spendable
balance like any other.
Created by its owner, disarmed, and never closed; the vault is never closed either. Field
order is the byte layout and is append-only — `reserved` exists so a later field does not
force a reallocation of every escrow.

types.name: EscrowArmed
docs: Emitted only when `armed` changes; setting the current value again emits nothing.

types.name: EscrowDeposited
docs: `position` and `position_pool` name the claimed position and its pool for `Fees`, and are
`Pubkey::default()` for `Wallet`. `balance_after` is the vault's token amount read back after
the transfer, so it equals the escrow's balance by construction.

types.name: EscrowFundingSource
docs: Where the USDC an `EscrowDeposited` records came from. The declaration index is the wire byte.

types.name: EscrowWithdrawn
docs: `amount` is never zero. `balance_after` is the vault's token amount read back after the
transfer.

types.name: FeeClaimed
docs: A fee claim. An `Active` position stays `Active`, in custody, and — if it was one — a tier
member; a closed position is paid its stored `accrued` and keeps its state. `fees_paid` may be
zero, exactly as `Withdrawn.fees_paid` may.

types.name: InstantSold
docs: The treasury buying a card off a holder at the live buyback rate.
**`observed_at` is carried because the attestation is not consumed here.** It is persisted and
read back later by the activation, so without the timestamp on this event there is no way to
audit after the fact how old the observation was that the pool eventually activated on;
`observed_age_seconds` at acceptance is carried too, so the acceptance-time and
activation-time ages can be compared directly rather than reconstructed.
`standard` and the four payer fields after it are **appended**, so no earlier field's wire
offset moves. This event and `DepositPending` are the only two that carry the discriminant:
those are the points where the value is derived, nothing rewrites it afterwards, and they are
the two an indexer sources it from when it inserts the position row.
`paid` is the seller's amount and `rate_bps` the rate it was paid at, whoever paid. On an
escrow sale `escrow_paid` is the loader's debit at `bid_bps`, and Treasury 03 received
`escrow_paid − paid`. On a Treasury 03 sale `escrow_owner` is `Pubkey::default()` and
`escrow_paid` and `bid_bps` are zero. An escrow sale emits no escrow event of its own, so a
`RebalanceEvaluated` after an in-place activation stays at this event's log index + 1.

types.name: NftClaimed
docs: `fees_paid` is the stored `accrued` the claim paid before closing the position, `0` when
nothing was owed. Appended last, so the earlier fields keep their offsets; a strict decoder of
the new layout rejects the earlier five-field payload rather than reading it as zero.

types.name: Pool
docs: A single pool's config, live counters, and accrual state. Seeds:
`[POOL_SEED, pool_id: u16 le]`. The `Pool` PDA also signs as its own vaults'
transfer authority.

fields.name: blank_faces
docs: Slots 0–2 below the ticket, slot 3 above it or 0, slots 4–7 always 0.

fields.name: t04_ceiling
docs: No longer read or written: Treasury 04's ceiling is `ProtocolConfig.t04_ceiling`, for every
pool. The field keeps its bytes so every later offset holds.

fields.name: blanks
docs: One count per `blank_faces` slot; 0 wherever the face is 0.

fields.name: escrow_bid_bps
docs: What an armed escrow pays for a card sold back into this pool, in bps of its value. 0 means
the pool has no escrow path; once set it stays within `buyback_rate_bps..=10_000`.

fields.name: treasury_04
docs: The protocol-wide Treasury 04, `PDA(["t04"])`. Default on a pool created before Treasury 04
was shared, until `consolidate_treasuries` writes it; no instruction that pins Treasury 04
can run on such a pool before then.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Zero, so a later field can be appended without reallocating every pool.

types.name: PoolCollection
docs: One admitted collection's record. Seeds: `[COLLECTION_SEED, pool, collection]`.
`collection` is the address read out of the presented asset itself, never a caller argument,
so seeding on it makes both a substituted record and a duplicate record for one collection
structurally impossible. `standards` is the bitmask from `common::standards`; the record
admits a collection *for* a set of standards, and a bit cleared today cannot reach a card
admitted yesterday because `Position.standard` is written once at intake and never re-read
from here.

types.name: PoolConfigArgs
docs: The genesis config a pool is created with — every parameter that lives on `Pool`.

fields.name: t04_ceiling
docs: Ignored, and kept so the args' wire layout holds: Treasury 04's ceiling is protocol-wide,
set by `set_t04_ceiling`.

fields.name: t04_ceiling
docs: Always 0, kept so the event's layout holds: Treasury 04's ceiling is protocol-wide.

types.name: Position
docs: One deposited NFT's custody + accrual record. Seeds:
`[POSITION_SEED, pool, nft_mint]`.

fields.name: standard
docs: Custody dispatch: 0 pNFT, 1 legacy `V1_NFT`, 2 MPL Core. Derived at intake from the
presented asset account's **owner program** and — on the Token Metadata branch, where one
owner program covers two standards — from `Metadata.token_standard` against a closed set,
then written once and never taken as an instruction argument: a caller-supplied
discriminant would let a depositor pick the weaker transfer path for a stronger asset.

types.name: PositionSeized
docs: A third party ending custody — the only position closure no bye.fun instruction initiates, and
the reason it must be logged at all: an unlogged one is indistinguishable from a bug.
`source_state` is on the event because it is the only way an indexer can tell which of
`close_seized`'s three effect sets ran. `owner_observed` is what the asset's `owner` read as at
the time, which on a transfer-out names the destination and on a burn or freeze does not.

types.name: ProtocolConfig
docs: Singleton protocol-wide configuration. Seeds: `[PROTOCOL_CONFIG_SEED]`.

fields.name: t04_ceiling
docs: The balance Treasury 04 is swept back to, in micro-USDC, for every pool at once. 0 until
the Administrator sets it, and `sweep_t04_overflow` refuses while it is 0.

fields.name: reserved_0
docs: Unused; zero on mainnet. The `reserved_*` fields keep the account's size and every later
offset.

fields.name: t05_authority
docs: The delegated $BYE-purchase key. Treasury 05 is this key's USDC associated token account,
so the authority is what the address is derived from rather than a second stored field —
`settle_roll` credits Treasury 05 on every roll and never debits it, and this key spends
it outside any instruction of this program.
Occupies the byte position Treasury 03's authority vacated (T03 is now a program PDA),
so the account layout is unchanged. Until an Administrator sets it, it holds the default
key and the derived Treasury 05 address is the default key's ATA.

fields.name: t05_authority
docs: Treasury 05's delegated $BYE-purchase key. Required and rejected at the default: Treasury
05 is this key's USDC associated token account, and an unset key would pin settlement
credits to an address nobody controls.

fields.name: t05_authority
docs: Treasury 05's delegated $BYE-purchase key, in the wire slot of Treasury 03's retired
authority.

types.name: RebalanceEvaluated
docs: The rebalance evaluation, emitted on every activation/exit/value-refresh trigger even when
the outcome leaves the blank set unchanged.

types.name: RollBatch
docs: One roll batch: the account the whole roll pipeline writes to.
Seeds: `[BATCH_SEED, pool, batch_id: u64 le]`.
**Field order is the on-chain byte layout.** Everything downstream of `commit_rolls` decodes
this account positionally. Every field before `expected_blanks` sits at the same offset in the
1,100-byte three-slot layout and in this one, and `bump` is the last byte of both, which is
what `close_batch` reads either size by.

fields.name: request_slot
docs: Timeout anchor for the 240-slot recovery window.

fields.name: caller_seed
docs: The batch PDA's own bytes, passed as the VRF request's `callback_args` — the globally
unique key `recover_batch`'s queue scan matches on.

fields.name: randomness
docs: Written exactly once, by the callback. One 32-byte value expands to all `n` draws through
the roll index `k`, so there is one VRF request per batch regardless of `n`.

fields.name: expected_w
docs: Running expectation of `W` and the blank counts, seeded from live state at this batch's own
`roll_index == 0` by `settle_roll`/`settle_roll_core` — not by `vrf_callback`, which could
seed it while an earlier queued batch was still moving `W`. Rolls `1..n-1` assert
`current == expected` *before* drawing; every roll rewrites both from its own draw and
rebalance afterward.
**Not a commitment snapshot.** The pipeline legitimately moves `W` between rolls, so a
snapshot would fail the batch at roll 1; a batch-local running expectation passes on the
batch's own mutations and fails on everything else.

fields.name: s_price
docs: Economic terms snapshotted at commitment; the buyback rate is deliberately absent.
**No `s_W`**: the draw reduces over live `W` rather than a range pinned here, and live `W`
is the modulus third parties reproduce.

types.name: RollOutcome
docs: What a settled roll drew. `None` is the value a `Pending` or `Refunded` roll carries — a
refunded roll has no outcome, which is distinct from having drawn a blank.
Declaration order is the wire byte — see [`BatchState`].

types.name: RollRecord
docs: One roll's commitment and result, inlined ten times into [`RollBatch`].
The draw inputs are persisted rather than recomputed so a third party can re-derive each result
from the batch account and position history alone, reproducing the randomness expansion
verbatim. `w_at_draw`, `n_real_at_draw` and `blanks_at_draw` are
the pool snapshot *at that draw*, which is not the snapshot at commitment: the pipeline removes
the drawn position and rebalances between rolls, so every roll after the first sees a
different pool.

fields.name: selected_mint
docs: Real-card result. `Pubkey::default()` when the roll drew a blank or has not settled.

fields.name: blank_face_idx
docs: Blank result: index into the batch's snapshotted `s_blank_faces`.

fields.name: draw_value
docs: `r`, persisted so the result can be re-derived.

fields.name: attempts
docs: Rejection-sampling attempts used, persisted so the fallback branch is visible.

fields.name: refund_reason
docs: `0` = settled. Non-zero identifies which refund branch was taken.

types.name: RollRefunded
docs: One roll returned to its roller instead of settling. No fee is split on a refunded roll, which
is why this event carries no split: the full ticket price goes back.
`reason` is the non-zero refund branch, matching the code persisted on the roll's own record —
zero is reserved there for a settled roll and so never appears here.

types.name: RollSettled
docs: One roll's terminal draw.
**The draw inputs are published, not just persisted.** A third party must be able to
re-derive this roll's result from the event stream alone, and the pool state the draw reduced
over is not the state at commitment: the pipeline removes the drawn position and rebalances
between rolls, so every roll after the first sees a different `w_at_draw`, `n_real_at_draw`
and `blanks_at_draw`.
**The fee split is published as its four destinations rather than as the two aggregates the
vault sees.** `fee_protocol` carries the integer remainder of the basis-point division, so
only the per-destination form lets a reader check the four against `s_fee` and confirm the
remainder landed where it is supposed to; the two aggregates are recoverable from these four
and are therefore not carried.

fields.name: selected_mint
docs: `Pubkey::default()` when the roll drew a blank.

fields.name: blank_face_idx
docs: Index into the batch's snapshotted `s_blank_faces`; meaningless on a real-card draw.

fields.name: fee_equal
docs: Stays in the vault as owed fees.

fields.name: fee_tier
docs: Stays in the vault as owed fees.

fields.name: fee_protocol
docs: Leaves the vault, and carries the basis-point division's integer remainder.

fields.name: fee_t04
docs: Leaves the vault.

types.name: RollStatus
docs: Whether one roll of a batch has reached a terminal, and which.
Declaration order is the wire byte — see [`BatchState`].

types.name: SeizureKind
docs: The observed cause of a third-party seizure, as `close_seized` established it.
`Burned` and `Transferred` are both *gone*; `Frozen` and `Undecidable` both leave the card
present and in the vault, and the four are separate variants because the remedies differ — a
burn cannot be undone, while a freeze, a transfer-out and a plugin holding up the move are all
reversible by the authority that caused them.
**`Undecidable` is the open-ended one, and it exists so the set does not have to be.** The
other three are facts: the account is gone, the owner is not the vault, a freeze flag is set.
This one is the absence of a fact — the asset's or its collection's plugin registry holds a
record whose effect on the `Transfer` lifecycle **this program cannot decide**: a `Royalties`
rule set that is an allow list or a deny list, an external `Oracle` or `LifecycleHook` adapter
that declares a Transfer check, an **asset-level** `BubblegumV2` plugin, or a `plugin_type`
byte a later `mpl-core` ships and this build has never heard of.
Each of those is narrower than the plugin it names: a `Royalties` record with
`rule_set: None` and a `BubblegumV2` record on a *collection* are both `Clear`. It is
deliberately *not* a claim that the transfer will fail; it is the statement that nothing
here can promise it will succeed.
**Which is why it is the one cause both of `core_asset.rs`'s gates admit.** The exits proceed
on it and get MPL Core's own verdict; `close_seized` accepts it as a cause. Enumerating
*decidable* gating mechanisms one at a time always leaves a position able to be refused by
both gates at once — unwithdrawable and uncloseable, holding live
`w_real` behind a card nobody can move. Enumerating the **inert** mechanisms instead and
defaulting the rest to this variant is what avoids that.

types.name: T03Transferred
docs: USDC moved from one pool's Treasury 03 to another's by the removed `transfer_t03`. Nothing
emits it now; it stays so the logs that instruction wrote still decode against this IDL.

types.name: T04CeilingOverflow
docs: A pool's Treasury 04 swept back to its per-pool ceiling. Nothing emits it now that Treasury 04
is shared and `T04Swept` reports the sweep; it stays so earlier sweeps' logs still decode
against this IDL.

types.name: T04CeilingSet
docs: Treasury 04's protocol-wide ceiling set by `set_t04_ceiling`, its only emitter. `old` equal to
`new` is a call that changed nothing.

types.name: T04Swept
docs: The shared Treasury 04 swept back to the protocol-wide ceiling by `sweep_t04_overflow`, its only
emitter.
`amount` is the excess that moved to **Treasury 03** — never the whole balance, and never a
protocol-revenue credit, so a watcher may reconcile Treasury 03's credits against this event
directly. A sweep that finds the balance at or below `ceiling` emits nothing at all, so every
occurrence of this event carries a non-zero `amount`.

types.name: T04Transferred
docs: USDC moved from one pool's Treasury 04 to another's by the removed `transfer_t04`. Nothing
emits it now; it stays so the logs that instruction wrote still decode against this IDL.

types.name: TierChanged
docs: Tier membership change: the member removed (if any) and the member added (if any).

types.name: TierEntry
docs: A single ranked slot in `TopTier.entries`.

types.name: TopTier
docs: Top-value ranking, sorted `value` desc, `activated_at` asc, `position_id` asc.
Seeds: `[TOP_TIER_SEED, pool]`.

types.name: TreasuriesConsolidated
docs: A pool's per-pool Treasury 03 and Treasury 04 emptied into the shared ones and closed, by
`consolidate_treasuries`, its only emitter. `amount_03` and `amount_04` are the balances moved,
either of which may be 0; `treasury_03` and `treasury_04` are what the pool names from now on.

types.name: Treasury03Migrated
docs: `Pool.treasury_03` re-pointed from a legacy authority-held account to the program PDA by the
removed `migrate_treasury_03`. Nothing emits it now; it stays so the logs that instruction
wrote still decode against this IDL.

types.name: VrfConfigChanged
docs: The four fields move together rather than through `ConfigChanged`'s per-field form: they are
protocol-wide, not `Pool`-scoped, and `ConfigValue` has no `Pubkey` variant. The slippage
bound travels with the venue because it is spent on that venue's fee and price impact — a
bound carried over to a differently-priced pool is the wrong number.

fields.name: old_max_swap_slippage_bps
docs: **Appended last**, so no existing field's wire offset moves.

types.name: WalletStats
docs: Per-wallet, per-pool rollup of active positions. Seeds:
`[WALLET_STATS_SEED, pool, owner]`.

types.name: WeightIndex
docs: One pool's real-position weight index: a Fenwick range-sum tree over `FENWICK_CAPACITY`
leaves with a LIFO free-slot stack. Not a PDA — a pre-created keypair account pinned by
`Pool.weight_index`.
